title: Control valve diagnostic context
text: Use position, controller diagnostics, pneumatic condition, process context and service history together. Treat friction/stiction, position deviation, abnormal load, supply pressure and device alerts as investigation signals, not standalone proof.
source: Knowledge_Docs

title: Process pump condition context
text: Use vibration, bearing temperature, pressure, flow and motor load together. Look for consistent multivariate changes and verify locally before maintenance work.
source: Knowledge_Docs

title: Electric motor condition context
text: Use vibration, bearing temperature, current/load and operating history. Prefer trend evidence over isolated thresholds.
source: Knowledge_Docs

title: Pressure transmitter validation
text: Assess continuity, drift, signal quality and comparison against process context or a reference measurement.
source: Knowledge_Docs

title: Vibration sensor quality context
text: Assess signal stability, drift, missing data and mounting quality. Poor sensor quality should reduce downstream confidence.
source: Knowledge_Docs

title: Field-service safety guardrail
text: The assistant must not replace site procedures, lockout/tagout, permits, OEM instructions or qualified personnel. Recommend verification and escalation rather than autonomous physical action.
source: Knowledge_Docs

title: Evidence-grounded AI response contract
text: Name the asset, cite telemetry/events/doc IDs, state confidence, distinguish observation from hypothesis, and propose the next safe verification step.
source: Knowledge_Docs

title: 3D scene-to-asset mapping contract
text: Map visible objects to stable asset IDs with explicit confidence. Mapping may use scene hierarchy, annotation, QR/NFC or computer vision. Never silently guess identity.
source: Knowledge_Docs

title: Baseplate (process pump, training note)
text: Baseplate: Common rigid frame that keeps pump and motor aligned. Typical symptoms: soft foot / loose anchoring → misalignment and vibration. Signals: vibration_mm_s.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Electric motor (process pump, training note)
text: Electric motor: Drives the pump; current draw reflects hydraulic load. Typical symptoms: current/load imbalance; overheating; bearing wear. Signals: motor_current_a, bearing_temp_c, vibration_mm_s, speed_rpm.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Flexible coupling (process pump, training note)
text: Flexible coupling: Connects motor shaft to pump shaft and tolerates small misalignment. Typical symptoms: misalignment → vibration (often axial / 2×); element wear. Signals: vibration_mm_s, motor_current_a.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Shaft (process pump, training note)
text: Shaft: Transmits torque from the coupling to the impeller; carries the rotating assembly. Typical symptoms: bending or run-out → vibration; fretting at fits. Signals: vibration_mm_s.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Bearing housing (process pump, training note)
text: Bearing housing: Holds the bearings and lubricant; a common mounting point for vibration and temperature sensors. Typical symptoms: lubricant contamination; loose sensor mounting giving poor data. Signals: vibration_mm_s, bearing_temp_c, signal_quality_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Outboard bearing (process pump, training note)
text: Outboard bearing: Supports radial and axial load at the drive end of the bearing housing. Typical symptoms: rising vibration; rising bearing temperature; lubricant degradation. Signals: vibration_mm_s, bearing_temp_c.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Inboard bearing (process pump, training note)
text: Inboard bearing: Supports radial load of the rotating assembly on the pump side. Typical symptoms: rising vibration; rising bearing temperature; noise. Signals: vibration_mm_s, bearing_temp_c.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Mechanical seal (process pump, training note)
text: Mechanical seal: Seals the rotating shaft where it leaves the pressurised casing. Typical symptoms: visible leakage at the seal chamber; seal-face heating; dry-running damage. Signals: bearing_temp_c, process_pressure_bar.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Impeller (process pump, training note)
text: Impeller: Rotating vaned wheel that adds energy to the liquid; its condition sets the pump's head–flow curve. Typical symptoms: fouling / build-up on vanes → lower flow for the same power; cavitation erosion at vane inlets; imbalance → vibration at 1× running speed. Signals: process_flow_pct, process_pressure_bar, motor_current_a, vibration_mm_s.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Wear ring (process pump, training note)
text: Wear ring: Small running clearance between impeller and casing that limits internal recirculation. Typical symptoms: clearance growth → efficiency loss, lower discharge pressure. Signals: process_pressure_bar, process_flow_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Volute casing (process pump, training note)
text: Volute casing: Collects liquid leaving the impeller and converts velocity into pressure; contains the discharge nozzle. Typical symptoms: internal deposits or fouling narrowing the flow path; erosion / cavitation pitting near the cutwater; external leakage at gasketed joints. Signals: process_pressure_bar, process_flow_pct, motor_current_a.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Frame and feet (electric motor, training note)
text: Frame and feet: Cast housing that holds the stator, carries heat to the cooling fins and bolts the motor to its base. Typical symptoms: Cracked or loose feet (soft foot) causing vibration; Blocked fins raising temperature. Signals: vibration_mm_s, bearing_temp_c.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Stator core (electric motor, training note)
text: Stator core: Stack of laminated steel sheets that carries the rotating magnetic field. Typical symptoms: Hot spots from damaged laminations. Signals: bearing_temp_c, motor_current_a.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Stator windings (electric motor, training note)
text: Stator windings: Copper coils that create the magnetic field when supplied with current. Typical symptoms: Insulation ageing from heat; Phase-to-phase imbalance in current. Signals: motor_current_a, bearing_temp_c.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Rotor (electric motor, training note)
text: Rotor: Squirrel-cage rotor that turns inside the stator field and drives the shaft. Typical symptoms: Broken rotor bars giving current sidebands; Imbalance raising vibration. Signals: motor_current_a, vibration_mm_s, speed_rpm.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Shaft (electric motor, training note)
text: Shaft: Carries the rotor and transmits torque to the driven machine. Typical symptoms: Run-out or bend causing vibration at running speed. Signals: vibration_mm_s.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Drive-end bearing (electric motor, training note)
text: Drive-end bearing: Supports the shaft at the load side, where belt or coupling forces act. Typical symptoms: Rising vibration followed by rising temperature; Noise. Signals: vibration_mm_s, bearing_temp_c.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Non-drive-end bearing (electric motor, training note)
text: Non-drive-end bearing: Supports the shaft at the fan end and locates it axially. Typical symptoms: Rising vibration and temperature; Lubricant degradation. Signals: vibration_mm_s, bearing_temp_c.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Drive-end shield (electric motor, training note)
text: Drive-end shield: Cover that closes the frame and holds the drive-end bearing in line. Typical symptoms: Worn bearing seat causing looseness. Signals: vibration_mm_s.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Non-drive-end shield (electric motor, training note)
text: Non-drive-end shield: Cover at the fan end that holds the non-drive-end bearing. Typical symptoms: Worn bearing seat causing looseness. Signals: vibration_mm_s.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Cooling fan (electric motor, training note)
text: Cooling fan: Shaft-mounted fan that blows air over the finned frame. Typical symptoms: Broken blades causing imbalance; Reduced airflow raising temperature. Signals: bearing_temp_c, vibration_mm_s.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Fan cover (electric motor, training note)
text: Fan cover: Guard that directs fan air along the frame fins. Typical symptoms: Dirt or debris blocking the air intake. Signals: bearing_temp_c.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Terminal box (electric motor, training note)
text: Terminal box: Where supply cables connect to the windings. Typical symptoms: Loose or corroded terminals causing phase imbalance; Moisture ingress. Signals: motor_current_a.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Valve body (control valve, training note)
text: Valve body: Pressure-retaining body with the flow passage and end flanges. Typical symptoms: External leakage at flanges; Erosion inside the flow passage. Signals: process_pressure_bar, process_flow_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Seat ring (control valve, training note)
text: Seat ring: Hardened ring the plug closes against; sets tight shut-off. Typical symptoms: Wear or erosion causing seat leakage. Signals: process_flow_pct, position_actual_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Plug (control valve, training note)
text: Plug: Moving part that sets the flow opening; its shape defines the flow characteristic. Typical symptoms: Erosion changing the flow characteristic; Galling causing sticking. Signals: position_actual_pct, stiction_index.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Stem (control valve, training note)
text: Stem: Connects the actuator to the plug and transmits the stroke. Typical symptoms: Scoring that damages packing; Bending causing friction. Signals: stiction_index, position_actual_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Bonnet (control valve, training note)
text: Bonnet: Closes the top of the body and guides the stem. Typical symptoms: Leakage at the bonnet joint. Signals: process_pressure_bar.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Stem packing (control valve, training note)
text: Stem packing: Rings that seal the stem against process pressure; too tight adds friction, too loose leaks. Typical symptoms: Visible leakage along the stem; Over-tightening causing stiction. Signals: stiction_index, load_for_opening_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Yoke (control valve, training note)
text: Yoke: Frame that holds the actuator on the bonnet and carries the position feedback linkage. Typical symptoms: Loose mounting giving position error. Signals: position_actual_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Diaphragm actuator (control valve, training note)
text: Diaphragm actuator: Air pressure on a diaphragm moves the stem against a spring; the spring returns it on air failure. Typical symptoms: Diaphragm leak reducing thrust; Weak spring changing the fail position. Signals: pneumatic_supply_bar, load_for_opening_pct, position_actual_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Diaphragm (control valve, training note)
text: Diaphragm: Flexible membrane inside the actuator that turns air pressure into stem force. Typical symptoms: Cracks or leaks reducing force; Hardening with age. Signals: pneumatic_supply_bar, position_actual_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Actuator spring (control valve, training note)
text: Actuator spring: Returns the valve to its safe position when air is lost. Typical symptoms: Fatigue changing the bench set. Signals: position_actual_pct, load_for_opening_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Positioner (control valve, training note)
text: Positioner: Compares the control signal with the measured stem position and adjusts actuator air. Typical symptoms: Calibration drift; Feedback linkage wear; Air relay faults causing deviation. Signals: position_setpoint_pct, position_actual_pct, pneumatic_supply_bar.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Process connection (pressure transmitter, training note)
text: Process connection: Threaded connection that brings process pressure to the sensor. Typical symptoms: Plugged impulse line giving a frozen reading; Leaks at the thread. Signals: process_pressure_bar, signal_quality_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Isolating diaphragm (pressure transmitter, training note)
text: Isolating diaphragm: Thin membrane that passes pressure to the sensor fill fluid while keeping the process out. Typical symptoms: Coating or corrosion shifting the reading; Damage from over-pressure. Signals: process_pressure_bar, sensor_bias.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Sensor module (pressure transmitter, training note)
text: Sensor module: Converts pressure into an electrical value; its stability sets long-term accuracy. Typical symptoms: Slow drift against a reference; Temperature-dependent error. Signals: process_pressure_bar, sensor_bias.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Housing (pressure transmitter, training note)
text: Housing: Two-compartment enclosure for the electronics and the field wiring. Typical symptoms: Moisture ingress through a damaged seal. Signals: signal_quality_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Electronics module (pressure transmitter, training note)
text: Electronics module: Linearises the sensor value and drives the output signal and diagnostics. Typical symptoms: Output fault or frozen signal; Diagnostic alarms. Signals: signal_quality_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Display cover (pressure transmitter, training note)
text: Display cover: Threaded window cover that seals the electronics compartment. Typical symptoms: Damaged O-ring letting moisture in. Signals: signal_quality_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Terminal compartment (pressure transmitter, training note)
text: Terminal compartment: Where the field cable is connected; separated from the electronics. Typical symptoms: Loose or corroded terminals causing intermittent signal. Signals: signal_quality_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Cable gland (pressure transmitter, training note)
text: Cable gland: Seals the cable entry against dust and water. Typical symptoms: Loose gland letting moisture reach the terminals. Signals: signal_quality_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Mounting stud (vibration sensor, training note)
text: Mounting stud: Threaded stud that couples the sensor rigidly to the machine. Typical symptoms: Loose stud damping high frequencies; Wrong torque changing the reading. Signals: vibration_mm_s, signal_quality_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Base (vibration sensor, training note)
text: Base: Flat base that must sit fully on a clean, flat machine surface. Typical symptoms: Paint or dirt under the base; Rocking on an uneven surface. Signals: vibration_mm_s, sensor_bias.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Piezo element (vibration sensor, training note)
text: Piezo element: Ceramic crystal that produces charge when squeezed by the vibrating mass. Typical symptoms: Ageing or overheating shifting sensitivity. Signals: vibration_mm_s, sensor_bias.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Seismic mass (vibration sensor, training note)
text: Seismic mass: Dense mass whose inertia squeezes the piezo element as the machine vibrates. Typical symptoms: Loose preload changing sensitivity. Signals: vibration_mm_s.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Housing (vibration sensor, training note)
text: Housing: Sealed stainless case that protects the element and shields it electrically. Typical symptoms: Damage letting moisture in. Signals: signal_quality_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Connector (vibration sensor, training note)
text: Connector: Top-exit connector for the signal cable. Typical symptoms: Corroded or loose connector causing dropouts. Signals: signal_quality_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: Cable (vibration sensor, training note)
text: Cable: Shielded cable to the monitoring system; routing and strain relief matter. Typical symptoms: Damaged shield adding noise; Cable whip from poor fixing. Signals: signal_quality_pct.
source: Industrial X-Ray AI educational knowledge base (non-OEM)

title: What Industrial X-Ray is
text: Industrial X-Ray is a browser pre-visit copilot for field technicians. It turns a 3D scan of an unfamiliar equipment room into a workspace: Explore the scan, Understand the cited diagnosis of an asset, Plan the maintenance with a virtual layout simulation, Practise on exploded teaching models (X-Ray, Learn, Practice), get remote Support from an expert, and see an illustrative Value calculator. The demo story follows a technician preparing to service pump P-005. It is decision support only: it reads data, highlights, plans and drafts; it has no connection to plant controls.
source: Industrial X-Ray product documentation (README / docs)

title: The 3D scan and its integrity
text: The 3D environment is a Gaussian-splat scan of an equipment room (Equipment Room.ply, 1,676,481 splats, all records valid). The browser renders 1,669,970 splats with view-dependent colour as compressed chunks; phones load the most important 730 thousand splats; a 2D floor plan replaces the 3D view when WebGL 2 is missing. The scan was rotated so the floor is level (RANSAC floor plane) and the walls are axis-aligned. Scale is treated as approximately metric (ceiling about 2.05 units) and was not surveyed. An earlier file, Industrial Boiler Room.ply, was corrupt from record 502,483 onward and is not used.
source: Industrial X-Ray product documentation (README / docs)

title: How the objects in the scan were found and labelled
text: Geometry first: splats with enough opacity are voxelised at 3 cm, floor, ceiling and four walls are fitted as planes, and the rest is clustered with DBSCAN into 676 object candidates, each with a gravity-aligned oriented 3D box. Then naming: a geometric/colour heuristic proposes a label, and a vision-language model (gpt-5.4-mini) looks at a context render and a close-up render of each box and picks one of 38 industrial classes with a confidence. When unsure it says 'other equipment' (260 objects) instead of guessing. 416 candidates have a specific type, 195 have confidence of at least 0.70, 7 labels were corrected in the team's AI-assisted visual review of renders (tagged review-corrected, not field-verified) and 30 are linked to workbook assets. Precision and recall have not been measured on a human-labelled sample; a check sheet is prepared for that.
source: Industrial X-Ray product documentation (README / docs)

title: How workbook assets are linked to objects in the scan
text: The 30 workbook assets have no real coordinates in the scan, so they are bound to compatible scan objects by a class-aware, one-to-one procedural mapping (for example a process pump to a pump-motor unit), preferring objects along the demo route; the target must be reachable by the robot. Every binding stores its method and a mapping confidence, which lowers the diagnosis confidence. On site, identity must be confirmed by tag, QR or NFC code before acting; a pilot would link assets through tags, QR/NFC codes or survey coordinates.
source: Industrial X-Ray product documentation (README / docs)

title: How the inspection robot plans routes
text: The robot is virtual. The floor is modelled as a height field on a 5 cm grid with several floor levels; obstacles are scan points between 0.12 m and 1.25 m above the local floor plus the footprints of extracted objects. A cell is walkable when it is observed floor and its distance-transform clearance is more than the 0.20 m robot radius. A* searches 8-connected cells with no corner cutting, a 0.18 m step limit and a cost that keeps the robot in the middle of aisles; line-of-sight smoothing shortens the path only inside walkable cells. An independent validation re-samples the route about every 2.5 cm and reports collisions (0) and minimum clearance. Block aisle adds an obstacle and re-plans from the robot's current position. Proximity: every asset within 1.2 m of the robot is framed and read out, forwards and in reverse. In the hosted demo the same planner runs in the browser as a JavaScript port.
source: Industrial X-Ray product documentation (README / docs)

title: How the diagnosis and its confidence are produced
text: An evidence engine (deterministic) gathers, for one asset: identity and current state, telemetry statistics comparing the last 12 hours with the asset's own first 24 hours and with class peers (z-scores), alarms matching the issue code or of high severity, work orders, historical service cases of the same class and issue, data-quality issues and documents. Hypotheses come from the equipment library and are linked to components; the leading hypothesis is shown with the alternatives. The workbook itself labels each asset's issue (for example FOULING for P-005 in Current_State); the copilot retrieves and explains the evidence for it, it does not discover the fault. Confidence is an evidence score, not a calibrated probability: model confidence x evidence support x (1 - data-quality penalty) x (0.6 + 0.4 x 3D mapping confidence); for P-005 it is 0.52. Maintenance priority = criticality weight x (100 - health) x model confidence, which makes P-005 the target. An LLM words the result following DOC-RAG-GUIDE and may cite only IDs from the evidence package; any other ID is removed by a citation checker. The checker verifies that each cited ID exists in the evidence, not that the sentence is fully supported by that record.
source: Industrial X-Ray product documentation (README / docs)

title: What the copilot can do and how it stays grounded
text: The 'Ask about the plant' copilot first applies transparent rules: find or locate objects in the scan, find the asset with an abnormal signal, find the faulty or highest-priority asset, open a diagnosis, send the robot, open the X-Ray view, Learn, Practice or the library. Other questions are answered from retrieved documents and the selected asset's evidence. With the backend running, a live LLM writes the answer and a checker removes citations that are not in the context. In the hosted (static) demo there is no live AI: answers are pre-generated by the same backend for common questions, or composed from document search. Every factual statement should carry a source ID in square brackets; the copilot gives no repair or disassembly procedures.
source: Industrial X-Ray product documentation (README / docs)

title: What data is real and what is synthetic
text: Real: the 3D scan of the equipment room. Synthetic: all asset data comes from the Valmet x Since AI builder pack, a synthetic 16-sheet workbook (Asset_Master, Current_State, Telemetry_Sample_3d, Alarms_Events, Maintenance_History, Historical_Service_Cases, Knowledge_Docs, Data_Quality and others); all 30 assets are classified SYNTHETIC and every record has a synthetic_record flag. Illustrative: the X-Ray teaching models, lessons and practice, the Value calculator and any example expert reply. Approximate: object labels, asset-to-object mapping, scale and the layout simulation. There is no live plant data, no historian and no CMMS connection.
source: Industrial X-Ray product documentation (README / docs)

title: What Plan mode does
text: Plan mode is a maintenance-planning simulation. The technician moves a virtual proxy of an object (in the demo, the hand pallet truck that blocks P-005's service area); the app checks collisions against object boxes and the occupancy grid, shows clearance from the distance transform and the service zone, and re-plans the robot route with the changed layout (in the demo 8.40 m to 7.98 m). The plan can be reset or exported. The scan itself is never changed. It is an approximate simulation, not an engineering clearance or installation check; the service-zone size is an assumed example.
source: Industrial X-Ray product documentation (README / docs)

title: What Support mode does
text: Support mode is an asynchronous remote-support hand-off. The technician pins notes on 3D locations, writes a question and shares a support package (link, code or file) that carries the pins, notes, plan, camera view and asset context. The expert opens it, adds pins and a recommendation (optionally starting from a cited AI draft that must be reviewed) and a draft work order, and sends a package back. There is no live multi-user session, no video and no connection to plant controls.
source: Industrial X-Ray product documentation (README / docs)

title: X-Ray, Learn and Practice
text: X-Ray shows an exploded teaching model of the selected asset's equipment type: process pump, electric motor, control valve, pressure transmitter or vibration sensor (49 components in total). Each component has its function, failure symptoms, evidence signals and fault codes, and a diagnosis highlights the suspect components. Learn gives guided lessons on the model; Practice is a scored exercise behind a safety check. The models are procedural and illustrative: not reconstructed from the scan, not OEM drawings, not a Valmet product, and the content is not certified training or a procedure for real equipment.
source: Industrial X-Ray product documentation (README / docs)

title: Work-order drafts
text: The copilot can draft a work order for an asset (inspection, priority from urgency, recommended check, evidence IDs, safety prerequisites: work permit, isolation and lockout/tagout, OEM or site-approved procedure, qualified personnel). It is only a draft that requires planner approval; it is never sent to a CMMS and it performs no control action.
source: Industrial X-Ray product documentation (README / docs)

title: How it could connect to plant data (design only)
text: Not built; a design note. Read-only adapters would replace the synthetic workbook without changing the copilot: OPC UA subscriptions and reads (never Write or Call) for current values and alarms; a historian read API for telemetry baselines; MQTT Sparkplug B subscriptions with the broker denying any publish to command topics; a CMMS or EAM read API for the asset register and work orders; a document-management read API for manuals. Each adapter maps external identifiers to asset IDs through a reviewed mapping table and attaches provenance (source, observed time, received time, synthetic, replayed or live). Stale or poor-quality data lowers confidence. There is no write path back into plant systems.
source: Industrial X-Ray product documentation (README / docs)

title: What a pilot would measure
text: None of these are measured in the prototype. A pilot would measure: object-identification precision and recall on a human-labelled random sample; the share of target assets located correctly in the scan; time to find a piece of equipment with and without the tool; time to prepare a maintenance visit; planning collisions or access problems caught before the visit; technician training performance; time to assemble a remote-support case and get an expert answer; start-up time and frame rate on standard laptops; technician confidence and usability ratings (for example SUS). It would also compare copilot suggestions with technician outcomes (agreement, false alarms) and use replayed real data before any live connection.
source: Industrial X-Ray product documentation (README / docs)

title: What is in the library
text: The library (book icon, or ask 'show me the relevant manual') searches every citable document: the builder pack's 8 knowledge documents (one core diagnostic context per equipment type, the field-safety guardrail DOC-FIELD-SAFETY, the evidence-grounded response contract DOC-RAG-GUIDE and the 3D mapping contract DOC-3D-MAPPING), 30 asset cards generated from Asset_Master and Current_State, 50 historical service cases, 49 component training notes for the illustrative X-Ray models (KB-XRAY IDs) and the product documentation of this prototype (DOC-APP IDs). No OEM manuals were supplied; the training notes are general knowledge, not manufacturer instructions. Every answer cites these IDs and a click on an ID opens the document.
source: Industrial X-Ray product documentation (README / docs)

title: The Value page
text: The Value page is a calculator with editable, clearly hypothetical inputs (technicians, look-ups per week, weeks, minutes before and after) and the formula shown. No savings are measured, and the app has not been benchmarked against Unity or any other tool.
source: Industrial X-Ray product documentation (README / docs)
